description: Bits to petabytes, decimal and binary modes.

faqs.a: Decimal (SI) uses powers of 1000: 1 KB = 1,000 bytes. Binary (IEC) uses powers of 1024: 1 KiB = 1,024 bytes. Storage makers usually quote decimal; operating systems usually show binary.
faqs.q: What is the difference between decimal and binary mode?

faqs.a: A bit is a single 0/1. There are 8 bits in a byte, so 1 Mbps is 0.125 MB/s.
faqs.q: What is the difference between a bit and a byte?

faqs.a: Yes — bits, bytes, KB/MB/GB/TB/PB in decimal mode, and KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB/PiB in binary mode.
